summary: Moldova's statistics bureau gives offenders by citizenship only as an all-offence count, and child victims, domestic-violence victims and trafficking victims by sex and age without citizenship. That is a weak citizenship proxy; ethnicity is recorded in the census but not in crime data.

nations.National (BNS, court administration, ant: Annual crime release; minor-victim court report; national trafficking report.

european_title: Not recorded by any Moldovan crime source
european_note: Moldovan crime statistics count only citizens of other states among offenders. Ethnic groups are counted in the census but not in any crime, victim or child-protection statistic, so neither ethnic Europeans nor any ethnic group can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Moldova records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

breakdown.why: The National Bureau of Statistics (BNS) gives only an all-offence count of offenders who were citizens of other states (307 of about 10,470 in 2025). The court administration's report on minor victims (56 child victims of rape in 2025) has age and sex, no citizenship.
Domestic violence victims (843 in 2025; boys aged 0-17 were 19.8% of male victims) by sex and age only; offenders by citizenship only for all offences.
No neglect statistics by citizenship or ethnicity.
113 victims of intentional homicide in 2025 by sex; offenders by citizenship only for all offences.

The 2025 national anti-trafficking report gives 108 identified victims (25 children: 20 girls, 5 boys) by sex, age, exploitation and destination country (52 adults exploited inside Moldova); the only citizenship given is 1 Turkish surrogate-mother victim. No trafficker citizenship.
Child pornography cases are counted without citizenship.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Moldova scores 9% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Official statistics give offenders by citizenship only for all offences, and child victims and trafficking victims by sex and age without citizenship. No ethnicity is recorded in crime data.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)
